guia.what: Hides content visually but keeps it in the accessibility tree. Use it to give an icon-only control a text name, or to name a region with a heading that takes up no space. It reuses the `ts sr-only` utility.
whenUse: There’s information the layout conveys visually that screen readers don’t get.
You want to name a region with a heading that won’t be shown.
Some context text helps explain a control outside its visual placement.
whenAvoid: You just want to hide something temporarily. That’s `display: none`, which does remove it from the tree.
The information is useful to everyone. Show it.
dos: Use it to complete what the interface conveys only through position or color.
donts: Don’t hide SEO text or content everyone should read in it.
Don’t use it to paper over a design problem. If something isn’t clear, fix the design.

nucleo: Only the CSS that visually hides content while keeping it accessible.
